sections.chapter_title: Forces and Newton's Laws of Motion
sections.title: The force concept and the free-body diagram
learning_objectives: Define force as a vector quantity with magnitude and direction.
Draw and read a free-body diagram for a body in a given situation.
Explain how a stretched spring can serve as a standard of force.

misconception.text: A body can exert a force on itself.

correction.text: It cannot. A hawk that accelerates while gliding is pushed by the air and pulled by the Earth.

signal.text: Our own question offers the body as its own source of force.

stem.text: Which of the following is a contact force?

explanation.text: Friction acts between surfaces that touch. The other three act at a distance.

stem.text: A hawk accelerates as it glides. What causes the acceleration?

options.text: The hawk's own wings pushing against the air
The force of the air on the hawk and the pull of the Earth
The speed the hawk already has

explanation.text: A body cannot exert a force on itself. The hawk is pushed by the air and pulled by the Earth.
